definitions.explanation: The act of delaying or deferring something to a later time, often with the implication of avoidance.

examples.japanese: {宿題|しゅくだい}の{先延|さきの}ばしはやめよう。
{問題|もんだい}の{先延|さきの}ばしを{続|つづ}けると、{状況|じょうきょう}はもっと{悪|わる}くなる。
examples.english: If you keep putting the problem off, the situation will get even worse.

notes:
{先延|さきの}ばし means putting something off to a later time, with a negative nuance of avoidance or irresponsibility. Unlike {延期|えんき} (a neutral, planned postponement), {先延|さきの}ばし implies the delay is unproductive.

WORD FORMATION:
{先|さき} (ahead, later) + {延|の}ばし (stretching, extending, from {延|の}ばす)

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {先延|さきの}ばしにする: to put off, to postpone
- {先延|さきの}ばしの{癖|くせ}: habit of procrastinating
- {先延|さきの}ばしをやめる: to stop procrastinating
- {先延|さきの}ばしにしない: to not put off

CONTRAST:
- {先延|さきの}ばし: putting off (negative, avoidant)
- {延期|えんき}: postponement (neutral, planned)
- {繰|く}り{延|の}べ: deferral (neutral/formal, often financial)
- {後回|あとまわ}し: putting on the back burner (negative, similar nuance)

NOTE:
Almost always appears in the pattern {先延|さきの}ばしにする. Using it as a standalone noun is less common.
